title: Valley Family Health Care notifies patients of breach of SSNs and medical data
date_note: Date of the notice letter ("November 18, 2026") in the sample filed with the California AG. The incident: a network disruption on 13 March 2026 per the letter and VFHC notice; the California AG listing gives 7 March 2026 as the breach date.
place: Idaho and Oregon, United States (headquarters city not stated)
summary: Valley Family Health Care, a community health center serving Idaho and Oregon, sent patients a notice letter dated 18 November 2026. It says a network disruption on 13 March 2026 led it to find that certain files may have been accessed and acquired without authorization; its review was complete on 9 October. Its notice lists names, Social Security or driver's licence numbers, medical and insurance data. It notified the FBI and offers IDX identity protection.
plain: A health center in Idaho and Oregon is writing to patients that files with names, Social Security numbers and medical details may have been taken after a March 2026 network disruption.
exec: Health-data breach at a community health center; identity-theft risk for patients and state breach-notification exposure.
action: Valley Family Health Care's letter offers IDX identity protection (enroll by 18 February 2027) and a call center at 1-866-200-0911 (Mon-Fri, 7am-7pm Mountain); patients should also review insurance and account statements.
impact: Number of people affected not stated in the notice.

sources.name: Valley Family Health Care notice letter (sample filed with the California AG)

validation.note: Primary: VFHC's own notice letter dated 18 Nov 2026 (California AG sample) and its web notice; the California AG listing records the breach (date 7 Mar 2026). ClaimDepot dropped as a tracker; its 48,269 count is not stated on any page read, so no figure is given.

review.note: Date unsettled: VFHC notice and CA AG listing carry no publication date; notice says notification completed 9 Oct 2026, breach 13 Mar (CA AG 7 Mar). The 18 Nov date rests only on ClaimDepot, so the event is probably older than the map window.
